deities: Shiva (crystal/sphutic Shivalinga - reported by Dainik Bhaskar as Asia's largest transparent crystal Shivalinga)
festivals: Shravan Mondays / Kanwar yatra (Dainik Bhaskar reports a two-day kanwar yatra from Mundara Dham to the Dighori crystal-shivalinga temple in Shravan)

history.period: Modern - established in the early 2000s (Alamy mentions construction around 2003)
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: seq 1832 (Mahakaleshwar Temple, Seoni) covers the Mahakaleshwar Mandir at the same Dighori village, likely part of this complex. MISATTRIBUTION FLAG: the CSV name 'Adi Shankaracharya Temple' is likely WRONG. Dainik Bhaskar (July 2025) reports the Dighori temple was established by the late (brahmaleen) Shankaracharya Swami SWAROOPANAND SARASWATI - the modern Shankaracharya title-holder of Dwarka/Jyotirmath who died in 2022 - not the 8th-century Adi Shankara. Alamy's 'Shankara Charya constructed a big Mahakaleshwar temple at Dighori' and 99mustsee's 'constructed by Adi Shankaracharya' appear to conflate the modern Shankaracharya with Adi Shankara. The complex (also called Gurudham Dighori / Guru Ratneshwar Dham / Pitrudham) is known for its large transparent crystal (sphutic) Shivalinga. Image is the Guru Ratneshwar Shivji Sphutic Temple at Dighori (curl-preflighted 200, image/webp).

name: Dighori Temple (Adi Shankaracharya Temple)
town: Dighori village, Seoni district (CSV town 'Seoni' is the nearby city, ~16-20 km away - documented at Dighori)
town_description: Dighori is a village on the north side of Seoni city (PIN 480882) reached via the Seoni Bypass Road. It is known for the Gurudham temple complex and the crystal (sphutic) Shivalinga temple, drawing Shravan kanwar yatris from the Mundara (Wainganga origin) region. Seoni city is the district headquarters of the Satpura-range region, also associated with Kipling's 'Jungle Book' country.

travel.road: Seoni Bypass Road to Dighori village, ~16-20 km north of Seoni (sources).

visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published in detail (verify - the Mahakaleshwar Mandir listing at the same village shows 07:00-19:00).
